about.title: Paradise Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and it happens more often than most Paradise residents realize — recent records show 3 traffic deaths and 45 injuries across 33 injury collisions in a single year, with Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up repeatedly on corridors like Skyway, Clark Road, Pearson Road, and Pentz Road. If you've lost a spouse, partner, parent, or child on one of these roads, California law gives certain family members and dependents the right to pursue a civil wrongful death claim separate from any criminal proceedings. That claim can address funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their companionship and guidance. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects grieving families in Paradise with an independent personal injury attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what a claim might involve, without pressure or obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Paradise Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Can Be Limited and Confusing
items.desc: California law prioritizes a spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible only in certain situations. An independent attorney can help sort out who has standing before time runs short.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Starts Quickly
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity — like a public roadway agency — may be involved. Getting connected early preserves options families may not realize they have.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Immediate Bills
items.desc: Under California law, recoverable losses can include funeral costs and lost financial support, but also the loss of love, companionship, and guidance that's harder to put a number on. An attorney can help a grieving family understand the fuller scope of a claim.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify under certain circumstances. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to clarify standing.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a family member in Paradise?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That deadline can be much shorter if a government entity, such as a county road agency responsible for a stretch of Skyway or Pentz Road, is involved, so it's worth asking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensation for the family's losses, even if criminal charges are also filed against the at-fault driver. The two cases proceed independently and have different purposes.
